comparison: Both address dynamic localization patterns during cell cycle (C135-C158, C163). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with detailed validation, while peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the impressive volume of data on heterochromatin dynamics. High agreement on the quality of cell cycle imaging data.

Both evaluate subdomain architecture findings (C9, C62, C103-C126). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong validation, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to specific inconsistencies between Figure 7 and supplemental data (e.g., XNP classification, ADD1 mitotic localization). Significant disagreement on data quality and interpretation.

Both address validation of GFP-tagging approach (C105-C107, C159, C202). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, confirming recapitulation of published results. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the validation controls without dispute. Strong agreement on methodological validation.

Both evaluate the screening approaches and experimental design (C3-C4, C58-C59, C63-C68, C70-C71, C77-C79, C82-C83). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes controls, replication, and validation rates; peer reviewers praise the well-designed, unbiased screens and novel data. Strong agreement on screening methodology quality.

Both address PEV validation and functional relevance (C60-C61, C92-C97, C100-C101, C172). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents 73-81% validation success; peer reviewers explicitly accept identification of genetic modifiers and functional contributions to HP1a complexes. Strong agreement on functional validation.

Both address proposed mechanistic models for subdomain formation (C12, C206-C207). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting models are speculative and require further validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating Figure 8 should be deleted due to lack of experimental evidence. Agreement that models lack support, with peer reviewers more critical.

Both address GO term analysis and candidate identification (C85-C87). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite unexpected categories, validated by 22 known regulators. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning criteria for distinguishing true hits from noise. Disagreement on interpretation of unexpected findings.

Both address multiple analytical methods and hit identification (C174-C177). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting minimal overlap between methods is well-documented. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning clarity in distinguishing signal from noise despite multiple methods. Disagreement on adequacy of hit selection criteria.

Both address overall complexity and novelty of heterochromatin organization (C11, C119, C200, C209). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting subdomains were previously described and lack of conceptual framework. Disagreement on novelty and paradigm shift claims.

OpenEval evaluates minimal overlap between screens and mechanistic interpretation (C80-C81, C186-C189) as UNCERTAIN, noting the upstream/downstream distinction is logical but not definitively proven. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates methodological considerations and caveats about PEV assay limitations (C164, C192-C199) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of limitations and recommendations for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these methodological caveats.

OpenEval evaluates methodological optimization and novelty claims for screening approaches (C165-C170, C173) as SUPPORTED, with validation through recovery of known components. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluates quantitative results and forward-looking predictions (C182-C185, C190-C191) as UNCERTAIN, noting interpretations are largely speculative despite clear quantitative data. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these predictive claims.

Partial overlap on localization data (C88-C91). OpenEval R1 rates screening approaches as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 rates localization findings as SUPPORTED but critiques disorganized presentation and selective application of assays. Agreement on data validity, disagreement on presentation quality.
